boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Simpson College customs, ceremonies, songs, and bits of campus lore.

cards.title: Move-In Day
cards.subtitle: Simpson College, Indianola
cards.notes: Arrive ready to meet the campus teams, Greek organizations, and residence-life communities that help new students move into Simpson.
cards.short_summary: A community welcome that starts at the curb.
cards.evidence_claim: Simpson says its sorority, fraternity, athletics teams, and residence life communities help new students and parents with move-in.
cards.access_notes: New-student arrival activity; confirm annual instructions with Residence Life.

cards.title: Campus Day
cards.subtitle: Simpson College, Indianola
cards.notes: Join a service project when spring classes pause for the day; projects take place both on campus and in the surrounding community.
cards.short_summary: A college-wide day set aside for service.
cards.evidence_claim: Simpson states that Campus Day, established in 1889, cancels classes for community-service projects on and off campus.
cards.access_notes: Spring-semester tradition; project assignments and participation details vary by year.

cards.title: Honors Convocation
cards.subtitle: Simpson College, Indianola
cards.notes: Watch for the spring ceremony that recognizes classmates whose work has stood out in academics, athletics, and community life.
cards.evidence_claim: Simpson identifies spring Honors Convocation as the ceremony that salutes students who excelled in the classroom, on the field, and in the community.
cards.access_notes: Held during spring; consult the college calendar for the current ceremony details.

cards.title: Lessons and Carols
cards.subtitle: Smith Chapel, Simpson College
cards.notes: Plan for an evening of readings and hymns in candle-lit Smith Chapel during Simpson’s traditional English Christmas celebration.
cards.short_summary: Candlelight, readings, and hymns in Smith Chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: Simpson says Lessons and Carols has been a college custom since the 1970s and is held with readings and hymns in candle-lit Smith Chapel.
cards.access_notes: Seasonal event; confirm the current performance date and attendance information with Simpson.

cards.title: The Sidewalk Seal Rule
cards.subtitle: Outside College Hall, Simpson College
cards.notes: Spot the seal embedded outside College Hall, then decide whether to sidestep it—the campus superstition links stepping on it to a failed test.
cards.short_summary: A finals-week superstition built into the sidewalk.
cards.evidence_claim: Simpson documents the belief that stepping on the sidewalk seal outside College Hall brings bad luck and causes a student to fail their next test.
cards.access_notes: Located outdoors outside College Hall; respect normal campus access guidelines.

cards.title: Walking Through the Gates
cards.subtitle: Red brick gates in front of College Hall
cards.notes: Notice the bookend ceremony: first-years enter through the red brick gates in fall, while seniors march through them again at graduation.
cards.short_summary: One set of gates marks the beginning and completion of a Simpson journey.
cards.evidence_claim: Simpson says first-years walk through the red brick gates in fall and seniors ceremoniously march through the same gates on graduation day.
cards.access_notes: Ceremonial participation is tied to fall opening and spring graduation events.

cards.title: Yell Like Hell
cards.subtitle: Cowles Fieldhouse, Simpson College
cards.notes: Bring your school spirit to Homecoming’s Cowles Fieldhouse pep rally, where campus groups present stomp-and-cheer routines.
cards.short_summary: Homecoming pride expressed through competitive stomp-and-cheer routines.
cards.evidence_claim: Simpson describes Yell Like Hell as an annual Homecoming pep rally in Cowles Fieldhouse where campus groups compete with stomp/cheer routines.
cards.access_notes: Annual Homecoming event; check current Homecoming programming for entry details.

cards.title: Mildred’s College Hall Lore
cards.subtitle: College Hall, Simpson College
cards.notes: Learn the documented 1935 College Hall tragedy behind a lasting piece of Simpson lore, and treat the location with care and respect.
cards.short_summary: A campus story rooted in a documented 1935 tragedy.
cards.evidence_claim: Simpson records that freshman Mildred Hedges died after falling in Old Chapel, now College Hall, and says the event remains part of campus lore.
cards.access_notes: Historical lore, not an activity; view College Hall only through normal campus access.

cards.title: The Carver Medal
cards.subtitle: Simpson College, Indianola
cards.notes: Follow the annual recognition honoring service and humanitarian leadership while reflecting on George Washington Carver’s time as a Simpson student.
cards.short_summary: An annual humanitarian-recognition tradition tied to Carver’s legacy.
cards.evidence_claim: Simpson says the annual Carver Medal honors an individual who has served and inspired their community while addressing humanitarian concerns.
cards.access_notes: Annual award and lecture tradition; verify the current recipient and event format with Simpson.

cards.title: Red and Gold, Then the Fight Song
cards.subtitle: Simpson College, Indianola
cards.notes: Listen for Simpson’s two signature songs: the Alma Mater, “Red and Gold,” and a fight song first printed in a 1939 college song booklet.
cards.short_summary: Two college songs with separately documented histories.
cards.evidence_claim: Simpson says Lucien Waggener wrote the Alma Mater, “Red and Gold,” and that the Fight Song first appeared in the 1939 Simpson College Songs booklet.
cards.access_notes: Songs may appear at college ceremonies and athletic events; consult current event programming.
